tasks.short: Receive consultation requests from other doctors, review the patient's record, examine the patient, advise the requesting doctor, and write the consult note.

steps.what: Requesting doctor enters the consult request with a structured question and urgency in the record
Internist receives consultation requests: by phone today, as electronic requests to read after the change, with urgent ones still phoned
Internist reviews the patient's record
Internist examines the patient with special or difficult problems
Internist provides consulting advice to the other doctor
Internist writes the consult note

tasks.design: Consultations are requested electronically in the record ({OTHER}) with a structured question and urgency, so routine requests do not come by phone. The consult view shows problems, medication, recent results and the question together. The consult note template starts from the question, and the internist writes the findings and advice as today. Examining the patient and advising the colleague stay with the internist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requests came by phone without a clear question, and data were gathered from several screens.
tasks.enabler_now: Records support electronic consult requests and summary views.
tasks.still_hard: Urgent consults still come by phone.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing the one finding the referring doctor missed.

evidence.claim: Records can carry electronic consult requests with structured questions and summary views.
The dossier is kept twenty years after the last change.

assumptions: Boundary: from the consult request to the consult note; follow-up care is outside.
Input contract: requesting doctors use the electronic request; fallback is phone.

Examining and advising keep their full time. s1 keeps 50 for reading requests and urgent calls; s2 keeps 60 because the consult view gathers the record; s5 keeps 85 because only the question and standard fields fill in. The requesting doctor's form (s0) is outside the internist's savings.
Requesting doctors fill the request in about the time a call took.
research_questions: Do consults happen sooner after the request?

incremental.description: Internist asks for clarification on vague requests.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: most consults are urgent and still phoned (s1 keeps 80) and the template saves little (s5 keeps 95) (12.1); high: most consults planned and requested electronically (16.4).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Review history, medication and tests before surgery, examine the patient, compute risk scores, decide the risk status and interventions, write the advice, check it, and send it to the surgeon.

steps.what: Internist reviews history, medication and tests before surgery
Internist examines the patient
Internist calculates risk scores: by hand today; after the change checks the computed scores against the examination
Internist determines the patient's risk status and recommends interventions to minimize risk
Internist writes the preoperative advice
Internist checks the final advice: risk, interventions and medication instructions against the examination, and the surgeon it goes to
Internist sends the checked advice to the surgeon in the record

tasks.design: A preoperative view in the record ({OTHER}) shows the planned operation, problems, medication and recent tests together. Published risk scores are computed by fixed formulas from the structured data, so the internist does not calculate them by hand. The advice template pulls in the scores and medication instructions. The internist writes the recommendation, checks the final advice and its surgeon, and sends it once in the record. Examining, judging risk and recommending interventions stay with the internist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Data were gathered from several screens and scores calculated by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Records compute published risk scores from structured data.
tasks.still_hard: Scores miss frailty that the examination shows.
tasks.human_edge: Advising that the operation should wait.
tasks.altitude: The internist judges risk instead of calculating scores.

evidence.claim: Published preoperative risk scores can be computed by fixed formulas from structured record data.
Decision software can be a regulated device; fixed published formulas here are not AI.

assumptions: Boundary: from the surgery planned to the surgeon advised; the operation is outside.
Input contract: structured data in the record; fallback is calculating by hand.

Examining, judging risk, recommending and the final check keep their full time. s3 keeps 10 for checking the computed scores against the examination; s5 keeps 70 because the template pulls in scores and medication instructions and the internist writes the advice; s7 keeps 20 for the send.
Surgeons read advice in the record as before.
research_questions: Do cancelled operations for missing advice fall?

incremental.description: No upkeep for the internist: checking computed scores is in s3's remaining time, and the record team keeps the formulas.

approvals.approved_version: The preoperative advice exactly as checked by the internist in s6, sent once in the record to the operating surgeon for this patient; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: complex patients have incomplete structured data, so scores are often done by hand (s3 keeps 60) and advice needs more writing (s5 keeps 85) (17.5); high: routine checks with complete data (24.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Lead ward rounds and direct staff, assign tasks and follow-ups, supervise students, and hand over at shift change.

steps.what: Internist directs nurses, specialists and other medical staff on ward rounds
Internist assigns tasks and follow-ups: by phone today; by entering them with role and due time in the record's task list after the change
Nurses mark tasks done in the record's task list
Internist supervises students and assistants
Internist hands over patients at shift change

tasks.design: Tasks from the ward round are entered as a task list in the record ({OTHER}), assigned to roles with a due time, so routine follow-ups are not phoned through. Nurses mark tasks done in the list. The handover uses a structured list generated from the record with open tasks and patients to watch. Leading rounds and supervising students stay with the internist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Tasks were passed by phone and handovers prepared from memory and paper lists.
tasks.enabler_now: Records hold task lists and structured handover views.
tasks.still_hard: Urgent changes still need a call.
tasks.human_edge: Teaching a student to notice a patient who is deteriorating.

reach.learn: Whether tasks are clear and on time.

evidence.claim: Records can hold role-based task lists and structured handover views.
Systems that log staff task completion need works council consent if used to check performance.

assumptions: Boundary: from the ward round to the shift handed over; nursing care is outside.
Input contract: staff read the task list; fallback is phone.

Directing and supervising keep their full time. s2 keeps 60 because entering a task takes most of the time a call did; s4 keeps 70 because the list replaces compiling open tasks, and the talk stays. Nurses' done marks (s2n) are outside the internist's savings.
Nurses read tasks in about the time calls took.
research_questions: Are follow-up tasks done on time more often?

incremental.description: Internist phones staff about urgent tasks not picked up from the list.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: staff still expect calls, so most tasks are phoned as well (s2 keeps 85), and the list misses tasks (s4 keeps 90) (2.6); high: staff work from the list (8.1).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Fill notifiable disease reports and death certificates, write medical status reports, check them, submit them to the authorities, and keep copies.

steps.what: Internist fills notifiable disease reports for the public health service
Internist checks the final notifiable disease report: diagnosis, lab results and dates, and the public health service it goes to
Internist submits the checked disease report to the public health service: by e-mail or post today, through the secure exchange after the change
Internist fills death certificate forms
Internist checks the final death certificate: cause of death, dates and the authority it goes to
Internist submits the checked death certificate to the municipality: on paper today, through the secure exchange after the change
Internist prepares reports on the medical status of individuals
Internist checks the final status report: findings against the record, only what the patient consented to share, and the requester it goes to
Internist sends the checked status report to the requester: by e-mail or post today, through the secure exchange after the change
Internist keeps copies of the reports in the record

tasks.design: Report forms in the record ({OTHER}) fill patient details, lab results and dates from the record, so the internist adds only the medical judgement (cause of death, diagnosis, functional status). Medical status reports share only what the patient consented to. The internist checks each report and its receiver and sends it once through the secure exchange to that authority or requester; copies are stored in the record.
tasks.previous_blocker: Forms were filled by hand from the record and sent by post or e-mail.
tasks.enabler_now: Records prefill report forms and send them through secure exchanges.
tasks.still_hard: Each authority has its own form.
tasks.human_edge: Judging the cause of death in a patient with many diseases.
tasks.altitude: The internist adds judgement instead of copying data.

reach.learn: Whether reports arrive sooner and complete.

evidence.claim: Records can prefill report forms with patient data and lab results.
Health data are special category data; sharing needs a legal basis or consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from the reportable event to copies kept; the authority's follow-up is outside.
Input contract: forms set up per authority; fallback is paper.

Medical judgement and the three checks keep their full time. s1 keeps 40 because the disease form fills patient details, lab results and dates; s2 keeps 60 because the cause of death is written by hand; s3 keeps 75 because only details fill in and the internist writes the status; each send keeps 20 for the release.
research_questions: Do notifiable disease reports arrive within the legal time more often?

incremental.description: Internist reports form changes to the record team.

approvals.approved_version: The notifiable disease report exactly as checked by the internist in s4, submitted once to the public health service for this case; any change needs a new check.
The death certificate exactly as checked by the internist in s4b, submitted once to the municipality for this death; any change needs a new check.
The status report, limited to what the patient consented to share, exactly as checked by the internist in s4c, sent once to the named requester; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: forms fill little for unusual reports (s1 keeps 70, s2 85, s3 90) and authorities still take paper (each send keeps 60) (21.5); high: standard reports with electronic exchange (41.7).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The internist keeps consulting, judging surgical risk, directing staff and making medical judgements in reports; phone requests, hand calculations and form filling shrink.
skills_to_grow: Using electronic consult and task lists
role.ambitious_version: An internist with more time at the bedside.
